_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-13 (late) · SkyRunner — the filter dropdowns were invisible, not missing.
_status: Two things closed. The Exhibit Adoption filters: you said they need dropdowns and don't all work — it turned out to be one fault, not two. The dropdowns were there the whole time, but a styling rule on the surrounding panel was cutting them off, so clicking a filter opened a list you couldn't see. Fixed. Calbright College Non-Credit was also being dropped from the District and Region filters because it was missing from our college list — 88 records' worth — and the sandbox college is now hidden. Second, the Common CR Reference is scoped and measured before any building. The honest headline: automatic matching can only ever handle about a tenth of it. Roughly 90% needs a person, because 'Racial Issues and the Police' and 'Community Relations' are the same academy topic written in completely different words, and no software finds that. So it should be built as a working queue for curators, not a matching engine. The encouraging part: the work is very top-heavy. The 50 most common recommendation wordings account for half of everything, and 1,593 of the 2,344 wordings appear exactly once. You don't have to boil the ocean.

items.text: Please re-open the Exhibit Adoption filters. All eight should now drop open properly when clicked — collaborative type, CPL type, sector, discipline, issuing agency, college, district and region. They are still tick-box lists so you can pick several at once; if you specifically want single-choice dropdowns instead, say so and I'll swap them, but that would mean losing multi-select.

One decision needed before the Common CR Reference gets built: should a canonical recommendation be one entry for the whole system, or one per credential? 83% of wordings only ever appear under a single credential, so per-credential is nearly free — but the most valuable ones appear under as many as 61 credentials, and those are exactly the ones worth canonicalising once.

Build the Common CR Reference as a ranked worklist, not a matcher — the measurement says automation reaches only ~10%. Rank topics by how much they collapse (wordings × colleges), offer group/split/confirm with curator attribution, and pre-apply the four automated rungs labelled by which one fired. Model the affordances on the CCR merge workspace. Read docs/common_cr_reference_scope.md first.

Before the CCR's next push, measure whether the CCR's own course distribution is as top-heavy as the credit recommendations turned out to be (top 50 = half of everything). If it is, the same work-the-head strategy makes the CCR tractable, and the 2,344-string CR Reference is the cheap place to prove it first.

The 'questions Sierra struggled with' list should now read about 13 instead of 78 — the rest was the automated test suite that runs on every deploy. Each row can be marked Handled or Leave it, and there is a bulk control for all of them at once. Marking does not change how Sierra answers; it only clears the list.

One decision only you can make. Eight colleges still show a contact from the old June snapshot even though MAP now holds nobody for them. They keep the old name so nobody is left with a dead end — but MAP is the system of record, and a blank there might mean that person left the role. Should those eight go blank instead?

QUEUED BY SAM as the next build: plan and create the Common CR Reference tab. Scope it against the CCR's actual matching factors first. His ruling stands — C-ID is one factor and not the key, because only about 17% of the 2,344 distinct recommendation wordings carry a C-ID at all, and the ones that do include a case (AJ 110) where the same C-ID sits on two genuinely different lines.
Twelve credentials are marked statewide in the adoption file but are missing from Sierra's credential table entirely, so she cannot find them at all. Carried for several sessions now.

Sierra's exhibit corpus still covers only 59 of 123 colleges, so a 'nothing found' answer at the other 64 is not evidence of anything. Worth deciding whether to close the gap or make the limit visible in her answers.

Seven fallback contacts were found by web search and the code deliberately refuses to propose them, because no session could open the pages to apply Jessica's sourcing rules. They render as 'Candidate — confirm' and still need a human or a differently-connected pass.

Still open from an earlier session: a site phrase currently opens its own tabs plus every shared CPL tab. That is only safe while everyone holding one is trusted with all shared CPL data. Worth deciding before the Finance phrase reaches anyone in Finance.
